facts_and_myths.claim: Satoru Gojo's signature blindfold was designed because looking at cursed energy directly causes physical blindness to the user.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Gojo wears a blindfold or dark sunglasses because his Six Eyes process sensory and cursed energy information with such infinitesimal detail that keeping his eyes uncovered at all times would quickly exhaust his brain.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Despite wearing an opaque black blindfold, Gojo's Six Eyes allow him to perceive high-resolution thermal and cursed energy signatures better than normal eyesight.

name: Spy x Family
visual_anchor: Elegant retro 1960s-inspired vertical 9:16 key visual featuring the stylish Forger family sitting on mid-century modernist designer chairs: Twilight in a sharp teal suit holding a folded newspaper, Yor in an elegant black dress, and telepathic Anya clutching her stuffed Chimera doll with mischievous peanut-loving smirks.
core_traits: Created by Tatsuya Endo and serialized biweekly on Shueisha's digital platform Shonen Jump+ since March 2019
Chronicles elite Westalian master spy Twilight, who assembles a fake suburban family named the Forgers to infiltrate an elite Ostania academy for Operation Strix
Centers on dramatic irony where neither parent knows the other's secret double life, while adopted daughter Anya secretly reads minds and family dog Bond sees the future
Achieved over 35 million copies in circulation, sparking massive global merchandising and widespread popularity for its wholesome blend of retro spy adventure and heartwarming family comedy

facts_and_myths.claim: Every single volume cover of Spy x Family features a real-world designer chair from iconic furniture history.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Tatsuya Endo meticulously illustrates renowned designer chairs on every tankobon cover, including Le Corbusier's LC2 for Loid, Charles and Ray Eames's Lounge Chair for Anya, and Mies van der Rohe's Barcelona Chair for Yor.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Endo has stated that he spends considerable research time studying classic modernist mid-century architectural and interior design to match each chair to its character.

facts_and_myths.claim: Anya Forger was originally designed as a high school spy partner rather than an adorable telepathic child.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Endo evolved Anya from a character named Ashe in his previous one-shot 'Rengoku no Ashe', but she was always conceived as a small eccentric child possessing clairvoyant or supernatural powers to serve as the comedic linchpin of the family.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Anya's iconic smirking 'heh' facial expression became one of the most widely shared anime internet memes of the 2020s.

name: One Punch Man
visual_anchor: Electrifying vertical 9:16 superhero poster featuring the yellow-suited Saitama with his red cape fluttering and crimson gloved fist thrust forward, unleashing a shockwave that splits atmospheric clouds in half while Genos and cosmic threat monsters loom in the fiery shattered cityscape.
core_traits: Created by ONE as a viral webcomic in 2009 and brilliantly remade as a manga illustrated by Yusuke Murata in Tonari no Young Jump starting in 2012
Subverts the superhero genre through Saitama, an unassuming hero for fun who grew so unfathomably strong that he obliterates any foe with a single punch, leaving him perpetually bored
Features the Hero Association tier ranking system (Class C to Class S), cyborg technology, monster disaster levels (Tiger to God), and Saitama's absurd mundane training regimen
Became a global sensation with over 30 million manga copies sold and a critically acclaimed first anime season animated by Madhouse that redefined modern action choreography

facts_and_myths.claim: ONE created the webcomic One Punch Man primarily as a quick digital drawing exercise to test web comic publishing software.
facts_and_myths.explanation: ONE started drawing One Punch Man using ComicStudio software in early 2009 simply to practice digital manga tools and storytelling pacing before the hilarious, minimalist webcomic went explosively viral across Japan.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Manga legend Yusuke Murata was so captivated by the webcomic while bedridden with illness that he personally reached out to ONE on Twitter proposing a fully illustrated manga collaboration.

facts_and_myths.claim: Saitama's overwhelming strength was granted by an extraterrestrial gene spliced into his DNA during an early monster encounter.
facts_and_myths.explanation: According to the lore explained by Dr. Genus, Saitama possessed no special lineage or genetics, but rather shattered his human 'limiter' purely through an obsessive daily routine of 100 push-ups, 100 sit-ups, 100 squats, and a 10-kilometer run.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Saitama's training regimen famously caused him to lose all his hair in exchange for boundless godlike strength.

name: Chainsaw Man
visual_anchor: Gritty cinematic vertical 9:16 poster of the Chainsaw Devil hybrid standing atop a pile of urban debris under neon Tokyo rain, bloodied mechanical chainsaws roaring from his head and forearms with spray and exhaust smoke, a starter ripcord cord dangling from his ripped collar.
core_traits: Created by Tatsuki Fujimoto and serialized in Weekly Shonen Jump from December 2018 to December 2020, continuing Part 2 on Shonen Jump+ since July 2022
Follows impoverished devil hunter Denji, who merges with his chainsaw devil canine Pochita to resurrect as Chainsaw Man and join Makima's Public Safety Special Division 4
Features a dark supernatural world where Devils are born from human fears, gaining strength from global dread and forming contracts with human hunters in exchange for body parts or lifespans
Surpassed 28 million manga copies sold and received prestigious Harvey Awards, celebrated worldwide for its subversive cinematic storytelling, unpredictable gore, and indie-cinema aesthetics

facts_and_myths.claim: The first season of the Chainsaw Man anime featured a completely unique ending theme song and custom ending animation for every single episode.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Studio MAPPA produced 12 completely distinct ending animations and commissioned 12 original songs from prominent Japanese artists including Kenshi Yonezu, Maximum the Hormone, Vaundy, and Aimer for each of the 12 broadcast episodes.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Tatsuki Fujimoto is an avid cinephile whose anime opening sequence contains over a dozen direct shot-for-shot homages to classic Western films like Pulp Fiction, The Big Lebowski, and No Country for Old Men.

facts_and_myths.claim: Pochita's canine chainsaw form was inspired by a mythical Japanese yokai dog from ancient Shinto folklore.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Tatsuki Fujimoto revealed that Pochita's distinctive design was inspired by a German handheld chainsaw tool and the lovable look of a small domestic puppy, intentionally contrasting adorable pet aesthetics with horrific mechanical violence.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Denji's modest initial dream was simply to eat toast with jam and cuddle with a girl, subverting traditional shonen grand ambitions.

name: My Hero Academia
visual_anchor: Cinematic vertical 9:16 poster featuring Izuku Midoriya in his green hero suit channeling glowing emerald One For All lightning bolts across his arms, framed against the towering golden silhouette of All Might smiling under dramatic storm clouds over the U.A. High School campus.
core_traits: Created by Kohei Horikoshi and serialized in Weekly Shonen Jump from July 2014 to August 2024, spanning 42 collected tankobon volumes.
Follows Izuku Midoriya, a quirkless boy born into a superhuman society who inherits the legendary One For All power from the greatest hero All Might to enroll in U.A. High School.

Revolves around Quirks, superhuman genetic mutations manifesting in eighty percent of humanity, countered by the hereditary stockpile quirk One For All and the villainous quirk-stealing power All For One.
Surpassed 100 million copies in circulation worldwide by 2024, becoming a cornerstone modern superhero anime franchise with multiple blockbuster theatrical films and global merchandising.

facts_and_myths.claim: Kohei Horikoshi originally conceived Izuku Midoriya as a quirkless gadget-wielding hero who would never receive a supernatural power.
facts_and_myths.explanation: In Horikoshi's 2008 one-shot 'My Hero', the hero Jack Midoriya used high-tech gadgets instead of superpowers to fight monsters.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Horikoshi is an avid fan of American superhero comic books, particularly Spider-Man, whose agility and web mechanics heavily inspired Deku's Blackwhip technique.

facts_and_myths.claim: All Might was originally planned to be an ancient demon disguised as a golden champion who manipulated Deku from the start.
facts_and_myths.explanation: All Might was always envisioned as the pure, unyielding Symbol of Peace and surrogate father figure inspired by classic Western superheroes like Superman, with no planned storyline depicting him as a demonic deceiver or covert antagonist.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: All Might's signature booming catchphrase 'I am here!' was designed to invoke immediate psychological relief for victims in disaster zones.

name: Death Note
visual_anchor: Dramatic vertical 9:16 composition showcasing the black leather Death Note notebook lying open with a crimson red apple beside a silver fountain pen, while the grotesque winged silhouette of Shinigami Ryuk looms ominously behind Light Yagami in shadows cast by neon police sirens.
core_traits: Written by Tsugumi Ohba and illustrated by Takeshi Obata, serialized in Weekly Shonen Jump between December 2003 and May 2006 across 12 tankobon volumes.

Chronicles prodigy high school student Light Yagami, who discovers a supernatural notebook dropped by a death god and launches a worldwide vigilante crusade to execute criminals under the moniker Kira.
Centers on the Death Note, an artifact governing human mortality by killing anyone whose name and face are known to the writer within forty seconds, balanced by the optional Shinigami Eye trade.

Sold over 30 million manga copies, sparked international psychological thriller debates, spawned acclaimed anime adaptations directed by Tetsuro Araki, and remains one of the most widely recognized gateway anime worldwide.

facts_and_myths.claim: The prototype pilot chapter of Death Note featured a magical Death Eraser capable of reviving people killed by the notebook.
facts_and_myths.explanation: In the 2003 Shonen Jump pilot chapter starring Taro Kagami, Tsugumi Ohba included a special eraser that could resurrect victims if their names were cleanly erased before cremation, but this tool was intentionally abandoned in the serialized series to ensure death carried permanent stakes.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Shinigami Ryuk's addiction to juicy red apples was chosen because apples aesthetically complement his gothic mouth design and evoke mythological forbidden fruit.

facts_and_myths.claim: L's true birth name was never decided by author Tsugumi Ohba and remains completely unknown to this day.
facts_and_myths.explanation: L's official canonical name was explicitly revealed in the official guidebook Death Note 13: How to Read as L Lawliet, written with the special character card included in the collector volume.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: L's peculiar habit of crouching on furniture was calculated to increase his cognitive reasoning power by approximately forty percent according to his own dialogue.

name: Haikyu!!
visual_anchor: Vibrant vertical 9:16 perspective of an orange-and-blue volleyball frozen mid-air at the apex of a net, flanked by a soaring black crow spreading feathered wings above Karasuno High court floorboards reflecting stadium lights.
core_traits: Written and illustrated by Haruichi Furudate and serialized in Weekly Shonen Jump from February 2012 to July 2020, totaling 45 tankobon volumes.

Centers on pint-sized spiker Shoyo Hinata, who aims to overcome his short stature by forming an electrifying setter-spiker partnership with prodigy Tobio Kageyama on Karasuno High School's volleyball team.
Grounded in realistic volleyball athletics, biomechanics, and tactical court formations, famous for the rapid-tempo Freak Quick spike attack and Karasuno's synchronized multi-man offensive rushes.

Exceeded 60 million copies in circulation, credited with driving a historic resurgence in youth volleyball participation across Japan, and produced a critically acclaimed anime adaptation by Production I.G.

facts_and_myths.claim: Real-world high school volleyball club registrations in Japan notably surged following the broadcast of the Haikyu!! anime series.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Official sports census data from the Japan High School Athletic Federation confirmed that boys' volleyball club enrollment experienced significant year-over-year percentage gains directly correlating with Haikyu!!'s peak broadcast and publication years.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Creator Haruichi Furudate played middle blocker during both junior high and high school, ensuring the manga depicted authentic court movements and tactical terminology.

facts_and_myths.claim: Karasuno High School was purely fictional and bore zero resemblance or connection to any real-world Japanese school or town.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Karasuno High School and its surrounding countryside were directly modeled on Karumai High School located in Karumai Town, Iwate Prefecture, which is creator Haruichi Furudate's real hometown and now serves as an active anime pilgrimage destination.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The Karasuno team motto 'Tobe' translates to 'Fly', matching their raven motif and black wing visual metaphors.

name: Tokyo Ghoul
visual_anchor: Gothic dark vertical 9:16 visual displaying Ken Kaneki's one-eyed leather zipper mask resting in a blooming field of crimson red spider lilies, glowing scarlet kagune tentacles curling upward against a rain-slicked Tokyo alleyway beneath a shattered crescent moon.
core_traits: Created by Sui Ishida and serialized in Shueisha's Weekly Young Jump from September 2011 to September 2014, followed by its sequel Tokyo Ghoul:re through July 2018 across 30 total volumes.
Follows bookish university student Ken Kaneki, who survives a deadly encounter with a flesh-eating ghoul only to be transformed into an outcast half-ghoul through an emergency organ transplant.
Features biological RC cells enabling ghouls to summon predatory organs called Kagune (Ukaku, Koukaku, Rinkaku, Bikaku), countered by the CCG investigators' forged Quinque weapons.

Surpassed 47 million copies in circulation worldwide, becoming a defining dark urban fantasy phenomenon of the 2010s renowned for its psychological depth, iconic opening song 'Unravel', and cult global following.

facts_and_myths.claim: Ken Kaneki's white hair transformation was biologically caused by the real-world medical condition known as Marie Antoinette syndrome.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Kaneki's sudden hair color shift during Yamori's brutal torture represents Marie Antoinette syndrome, an acute physical condition where extreme emotional trauma, stress, and cell damage cause hair to rapidly lose pigmentation and turn white.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Kaneki's habit of cracking his knuckles with his thumb was psychological mimicry unconsciously inherited from his torturer Yamori, who had originally stolen it from his own prison interrogator.

facts_and_myths.claim: Sui Ishida was an established veteran manga author who published several successful long-running series under a famous pen name before Tokyo Ghoul.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Tokyo Ghoul was Sui Ishida's debut commercial serialization after winning a Rookie Manga Award in Young Jump in 2010; he had only drawn webcomics previously and kept his personal identity completely anonymous.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Ishida personally illustrated over a thousand unique chapter title splash pages and bonus art cards throughout the franchise's weekly run.

name: JoJo's Bizarre Adventure
visual_anchor: High-fashion vertical 9:16 pop-art poster highlighting an ancient Aztec Stone Mask dripping with crimson mist beside a golden star-shaped Joestar birthmark, framed by jagged vibrant purple Japanese onomatopoeia 'Menacing' characters and flamboyant dynamic posture silhouettes.
core_traits: Created by Hirohiko Araki and serialized in Weekly Shonen Jump starting December 1986 before transitioning to Ultra Jump in 2005, spanning over 130 tankobon volumes across multiple narrative parts.
Spans generations of the heroic Joestar bloodline, each nicknamed JoJo, battling supernatural vampires, ancient beings, and enemy Stand users across distinct historical eras and global settings.
Pioneered the concept of Stands—physical manifestations of spiritual life energy with bespoke supernatural abilities—succeeding the ancient martial art of solar breathing known as Ripple or Hamon.

Over 120 million copies in circulation, celebrated internationally for its flamboyant high-fashion aesthetics, Louvre museum collaborations, iconic poses, and pervasive influence on contemporary gaming and manga culture.

facts_and_myths.claim: Hirohiko Araki had his original artwork exhibited in the Louvre Museum in Paris as part of an official collaborative comic collection.
facts_and_myths.explanation: In 2009, Araki created 'Rohan at the Louvre' for the Musee du Louvre's prestigious comic art exhibition project, making JoJo's Bizarre Adventure the first manga series ever officially featured and exhibited inside the historic Parisian institution.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Araki named dozens of characters and Stands after Western rock, pop, and jazz musicians, including Led Zeppelin, Queen, Prince, and AC/DC.

facts_and_myths.claim: Stands were introduced in Part 1 Phantom Blood from the very beginning of the series.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Parts 1 and 2 (Phantom Blood and Battle Tendency) relied entirely on the solar energy breathing technique known as Hamon (the Ripple) alongside vampiric stone masks; Stands were only introduced later in Part 3 (Stardust Crusaders) in 1989.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The word 'Stand' comes from the phrase 'standing by me', describing a spirit avatar standing alongside its user.

name: Bulbasaur
visual_anchor: A cheerful Bulbasaur with blue-green skin and a big green plant bulb on its back, standing in a sunny meadow full of flowers, 9:16 vertical shot.
core_traits: Small blue-green Pokemon that walks on four legs
Carries a big plant bulb on its back
Grass-type starter Pokemon in Pokemon Red and Blue
Number 001 in the National Pokedex and evolves into Ivysaur

facts_and_myths.claim: Bulbasaur is the very first Pokemon in the National Pokedex.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Bulbasaur holds number 001, so it appears first when you open the National Pokedex.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Bulbasaur grows into Ivysaur and then into the big flowering Venusaur.

facts_and_myths.claim: The bulb on Bulbasaur's back is just a decoration.
facts_and_myths.explanation: The Pokedex says a seed sits on its back from birth and grows larger as Bulbasaur grows.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Bulbasaur naps in bright sunlight, and soaking up the sun's rays helps its seed grow.

name: Charmander
visual_anchor: A friendly orange Charmander with a bright flame burning on the tip of its tail, smiling on a warm rocky hillside at sunset, 9:16 vertical shot.
core_traits: Small orange lizard-like Pokemon
Has a flame burning at the tip of its tail
Fire-type starter Pokemon in Pokemon Red and Blue
Evolves into Charmeleon and later Charizard

facts_and_myths.claim: Charmander likes hot places.
facts_and_myths.explanation: The Pokedex says Charmander prefers hot places, and steam rises from its tail when it rains.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: In the anime, Ash's Charmander grew all the way up into a mighty Charizard.

facts_and_myths.claim: Charmander is a Dragon-type Pokemon.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Charmander is a pure Fire-type. Even its final form, Charizard, is Fire and Flying, not Dragon.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Charmander is number 004 in the National Pokedex.

name: Squirtle
visual_anchor: A happy light-blue Squirtle with a round brown shell, splashing in a sparkling pond under a spray of water droplets, 9:16 vertical shot.
core_traits: Small light-blue turtle Pokemon with a curly tail
Has a hard brown shell on its back
Water-type starter Pokemon in Pokemon Red and Blue
Evolves into Wartortle and later Blastoise

facts_and_myths.claim: Squirtle can pull its head into its shell to stay safe.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Like a real turtle, Squirtle tucks its long neck into its shell for protection.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: In the anime, Ash's Squirtle once led the Squirtle Squad, a gang wearing cool sunglasses.

facts_and_myths.claim: Squirtle evolves straight into Blastoise.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Squirtle first evolves into Wartortle, and Wartortle later evolves into Blastoise.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Squirtle's name mixes the words 'squirt' and 'turtle.'

name: Eevee
visual_anchor: A fluffy brown Eevee with a cream-colored furry collar and big ears, sitting happily among colorful autumn leaves, 9:16 vertical shot.
core_traits: Small fox-like Pokemon with brown fur
Has a fluffy cream collar and a bushy tail
Normal-type Pokemon famous for its many evolutions
Partner Pokemon in Pokemon: Let's Go, Eevee!

facts_and_myths.claim: Eevee can evolve into eight different Pokemon.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Eevee's evolutions are Vaporeon, Jolteon, Flareon, Espeon, Umbreon, Leafeon, Glaceon and Sylveon.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Fans call Eevee's evolutions 'Eeveelutions.'

facts_and_myths.claim: Every Eevee always evolves into the same Pokemon.
facts_and_myths.explanation: What Eevee becomes depends on things like evolution stones, friendship, time of day, or where it levels up.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: In the anime, Ash's rival Gary had an Eevee that evolved into Umbreon.

name: Jigglypuff
visual_anchor: A round pink Jigglypuff with big blue eyes and a curl of fur on its head, singing into a microphone on a small sparkly stage, 9:16 vertical shot.
core_traits: Round, pink, balloon-shaped Pokemon
Has big blue eyes and a curl of fur on its head
Sings a lullaby that makes listeners fall asleep
In the anime it doodles on faces when its audience dozes off

facts_and_myths.claim: Jigglypuff's song can make listeners fall asleep.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Jigglypuff's famous move is Sing, a soothing lullaby that sends listeners off to dreamland.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Jigglypuff has been a playable fighter in every Super Smash Bros. game.

facts_and_myths.claim: Jigglypuff is happy when everyone falls asleep during its song.
facts_and_myths.explanation: In the anime, Jigglypuff gets upset when its audience dozes off and doodles on their faces with a marker.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Jigglypuff evolves into Wigglytuff when it is exposed to a Moon Stone.

name: Snorlax
visual_anchor: A huge, sleepy dark-teal Snorlax with a big cream belly, napping peacefully across a sunny forest path, 9:16 vertical shot.
core_traits: Huge, round, very sleepy Pokemon
Has a dark teal body and a big cream-colored belly
Spends most of its day eating and sleeping
Blocks the road in Pokemon Red and Blue until woken with the Poke Flute

facts_and_myths.claim: Snorlax eats about 400 kilograms of food every day.
facts_and_myths.explanation: The Pokedex says Snorlax is not satisfied until it eats about 400 kilograms, or 880 pounds, of food daily.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Snorlax weighs about 460 kilograms, the heaviest of the original 151 Pokemon.

facts_and_myths.claim: You can wake a sleeping Snorlax by pushing it out of the way.
facts_and_myths.explanation: In Pokemon Red and Blue, players must play the Poke Flute to wake Snorlax so it moves.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Snorlax has a baby form called Munchlax, which is always hungry too.

name: Psyduck
visual_anchor: A yellow Psyduck holding its head with both hands and looking puzzled, standing beside a calm blue lake, 9:16 vertical shot.
core_traits: Yellow duck-like Pokemon
Often holds its head because of headaches
Uses mysterious powers when its headache gets too strong
Evolves into Golduck

facts_and_myths.claim: Psyduck is a Psychic-type Pokemon.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Despite its name and its strange powers, Psyduck is a Water-type Pokemon.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: In the anime, Misty's Psyduck often popped out of its Poke Ball by surprise.

facts_and_myths.claim: Psyduck's headaches can trigger mysterious psychic powers.
facts_and_myths.explanation: The Pokedex says that when Psyduck's headache becomes intense, it starts using mysterious powers.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Psyduck always looks puzzled because it can't remember using its powers.

name: Togepi
visual_anchor: A tiny Togepi peeking out of a white eggshell decorated with red and blue triangles, sitting on soft grass among daisies, 9:16 vertical shot.
core_traits: Tiny baby Pokemon with a little crown of spikes on its head
Its body stays inside a white eggshell with colorful triangles
Misty's Togepi hatched from an egg Ash found in the anime
Evolves into Togetic when it becomes very friendly with its trainer

facts_and_myths.claim: Togepi is said to share good luck when treated kindly.
facts_and_myths.explanation: The Pokedex says Togepi's shell is filled with joy, and it shares good luck with kind people.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Togepi appeared in the anime before the Pokemon Gold and Silver games came out.

facts_and_myths.claim: Togepi has always been a Fairy-type Pokemon.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Togepi started as a Normal-type and became Fairy-type when Pokemon X and Y added the Fairy type.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Togepi's final evolution, Togekiss, evolves from Togetic using a Shiny Stone.

name: Meowth
visual_anchor: A cream-colored Meowth with a shiny gold coin on its forehead, standing on its hind legs and grinning playfully on a sunny city street, 9:16 vertical shot.
core_traits: Cream-colored cat Pokemon
Has a shiny gold coin on its forehead
Team Rocket's Meowth walks on two legs and talks like a person
Evolves into Persian

facts_and_myths.claim: Every Meowth can talk like a human.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Only Team Rocket's Meowth in the anime taught itself human words. Other Meowth just say 'Meowth!'
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Team Rocket's Meowth also taught itself to walk on two legs like a person.

facts_and_myths.claim: Meowth loves shiny, round things like coins.
facts_and_myths.explanation: The Pokedex says Meowth adores round objects and wanders at night looking for dropped coins.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Meowth's move Pay Day scatters coins that trainers can collect afterward.

name: Lucario
visual_anchor: A blue-and-black Lucario standing tall on a misty mountaintop at sunrise, a calm blue aura glowing softly around its paws, 9:16 vertical shot.
core_traits: Blue and black jackal-like Pokemon that stands on two legs
Has spikes on the backs of its paws and on its chest
Can sense and control aura
Evolves from Riolu

facts_and_myths.claim: Lucario can sense the aura of people and Pokemon.
facts_and_myths.explanation: The Pokedex says Lucario catches the aura flowing from others to read their thoughts and movements.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Lucario starred in the 2005 movie Lucario and the Mystery of Mew.

facts_and_myths.claim: Lucario evolves into Riolu.
facts_and_myths.explanation: It is the other way around: Riolu evolves into Lucario when it is very friendly with its trainer during the day.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Lucario has been a playable fighter in Super Smash Bros. since Brawl.

name: Shizuka Minamoto
visual_anchor: A cheerful cartoon schoolgirl with short dark pigtails and a pink dress, holding a violin in a sunny Japanese neighborhood park, 9:16 vertical shot.
core_traits: Kind and cheerful girl in a famous robot-cat cartoon
Nobita's friend and classmate who studies hard
Takes violin lessons
Her favorite snack is roasted sweet potatoes

facts_and_myths.claim: Shizuka takes violin lessons in Doraemon.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Shizuka practices the violin, though her squeaky playing is a running joke in the series.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: In the 2014 English version of Doraemon, Shizuka is called Sue.

facts_and_myths.claim: Shizuka is Nobita's sister.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Shizuka is Nobita's friend and classmate. Nobita is an only child who lives with his parents.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Shizuka gets much better grades than Nobita and often studies with him.

name: Gian
visual_anchor: A big, sturdy cartoon boy in an orange shirt singing loudly into a microphone on a small backyard stage while his friends laugh and cover their ears, 9:16 vertical shot.
core_traits: Big, strong kid in a famous robot-cat cartoon
Bossy leader of the neighborhood kids
Loves to sing, but his singing is famously off-key
Helps at his family's grocery store and has a little sister named Jaiko

facts_and_myths.claim: Gian loves to sing, but his songs are famously off-key.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Gian dreams of being a singer, and his loud concerts make his friends cover their ears.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: In the 2014 English version of Doraemon, Gian is called Big G.

facts_and_myths.claim: Gian is the smartest kid in Nobita's class.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Gian is the strongest kid, not the smartest. The top student in the class is Dekisugi.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Gian's real name is Takeshi Goda; 'Gian' is just his nickname.

name: Suneo Honekawa
visual_anchor: A short cartoon boy with spiky swept-back hair in a neat shirt, proudly showing off a shiny model airplane in a sunny park, 9:16 vertical shot.
core_traits: Short kid with pointy, swept-back hair
Comes from a rich family and loves to show off
Often tags along with the big kid Gian
Loves building plastic model kits

facts_and_myths.claim: Suneo often shows off his new toys and games.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Suneo's family is wealthy, and he loves bragging about his latest toys, games and trips.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: In the 2014 English version of Doraemon, Suneo is called Sneech.

facts_and_myths.claim: Suneo is the tallest kid in his friend group.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Suneo is actually quite short, especially when he stands next to his big friend Gian.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Suneo loves building detailed plastic models of planes and ships.

name: Dorami
visual_anchor: A small yellow robot cat with round ears topped by a red bow, smiling and holding a golden melon bread bun in a bright futuristic room, 9:16 vertical shot.
core_traits: Small yellow robot cat from the future
Has ears with a red ribbon bow
Little sister of a famous blue robot cat
Her favorite snack is melon bread

facts_and_myths.claim: Dorami is Doraemon's older sister.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Dorami is Doraemon's younger sister, though she is often more careful and reliable than him.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Unlike her big brother, Dorami still has her ears.

facts_and_myths.claim: Dorami's favorite food is melon bread.
facts_and_myths.explanation: While Doraemon loves dorayaki pancakes, Dorami's favorite treat is sweet melon bread.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Dorami is yellow, the same color Doraemon was before he turned blue.

name: Anywhere Door
visual_anchor: A bright pink door standing all by itself in a grassy field, half open to reveal a sunny tropical beach on the other side, 9:16 vertical shot.
core_traits: Magical gadget from a robot cat's pocket
Looks like an ordinary pink door standing by itself
Open it and you step into the place you imagine
One of the most famous gadgets in Doraemon

facts_and_myths.claim: The Anywhere Door can take you to almost any place you imagine.
facts_and_myths.explanation: You think of a place, open the door, and step right through to get there.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Doraemon pulls the Anywhere Door out of his magical four-dimensional pocket.

facts_and_myths.claim: The Anywhere Door lets you travel back in time.
facts_and_myths.explanation: It only moves you to other places. For time travel, Doraemon uses the Time Machine in Nobita's desk drawer.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Fans in Japan often name the Anywhere Door as the Doraemon gadget they most want.

name: Bamboo-Copter
visual_anchor: A cheerful cartoon boy flying over rooftops with a small yellow propeller gadget on top of his head, bright blue sky with fluffy clouds, 9:16 vertical shot.
core_traits: Tiny gadget from a robot cat's pocket
Looks like a little propeller
Stick it on your head and you can fly
Doraemon and his friends often use it to fly off on adventures

facts_and_myths.claim: You wear the Bamboo-Copter on your head to fly.
facts_and_myths.explanation: The small propeller spins on top of your head and lifts you up into the sky.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The Bamboo-Copter is one of the gadgets Doraemon uses most often.

facts_and_myths.claim: The Bamboo-Copter can fly forever without a rest.
facts_and_myths.explanation: In the stories, its battery runs low if it is used too long, so riders must land and let it rest.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Doraemon carries spare Bamboo-Copters so all his friends can fly together.

name: Ponyo
visual_anchor: A cheerful little red goldfish girl with a round human face, swimming among bubbles and glowing jellyfish in a sparkling blue sea, 9:16 vertical shot.
core_traits: Little red fish with a human-like face
Becomes friends with a five-year-old boy named Sosuke
Wishes to become a human girl
Loves eating ham

facts_and_myths.claim: Ponyo loves eating ham.
facts_and_myths.explanation: When Sosuke shares his ham sandwich, Ponyo discovers that ham is her favorite food.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Ponyo's father named her Brunhilde, but she prefers the name Ponyo.

facts_and_myths.claim: The movie Ponyo was made by Disney.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Ponyo was made by Studio Ghibli and directed by Hayao Miyazaki. Disney helped release the English version.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The movie's full Japanese title means 'Ponyo on the Cliff by the Sea.'

name: Catbus
visual_anchor: A giant fluffy orange-striped cat shaped like a bus, with a wide friendly smile and glowing headlight eyes, bounding through a starry countryside, 9:16 vertical shot.
core_traits: Giant fluffy cat shaped like a bus
Has many legs and a big friendly grin
Appears in My Neighbor Totoro
Its glowing eyes work like headlights

facts_and_myths.claim: The Catbus has twelve legs.
facts_and_myths.explanation: In My Neighbor Totoro, the Catbus races across fields and treetops on twelve furry legs.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The Ghibli Museum in Japan has a soft Catbus that young kids can climb on.

facts_and_myths.claim: The Catbus is a normal bus with a cat driver.
facts_and_myths.explanation: The Catbus is itself a giant cat. Passengers ride inside its soft, furry body.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The sign on the Catbus's head changes to show where it is going.

name: Soot Sprites
visual_anchor: Dozens of tiny round fuzzy black soot sprites with big white eyes, each holding a colorful star-shaped candy in a cozy wooden room, 9:16 vertical shot.
core_traits: Tiny, round, fuzzy black balls with big eyes
Live in dusty, empty old houses
Appear in My Neighbor Totoro
Carry lumps of coal in Spirited Away

facts_and_myths.claim: Soot sprites appear in two Studio Ghibli movies.
facts_and_myths.explanation: They show up in My Neighbor Totoro and again in Spirited Away, working in Kamaji's boiler room.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: In Spirited Away, the soot sprites love munching tiny star-shaped candies.

facts_and_myths.claim: Soot sprites like to stay in houses full of happy people.
facts_and_myths.explanation: In My Neighbor Totoro, the soot sprites quietly move out once kind, cheerful people move in.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Their Japanese name, susuwatari, means something like 'drifting soot.'

name: Jiji
visual_anchor: A small black cat with big round eyes perched on the end of a flying broom above a seaside town with red rooftops, 9:16 vertical shot.
core_traits: Small black cat with big round eyes
Best friend and travel buddy of a young witch
Can talk, but only his witch friend understands him
From Kiki's Delivery Service

facts_and_myths.claim: Everyone in town can understand Jiji when he talks.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Only Kiki can understand Jiji. To everyone else, he sounds like an ordinary cat meowing.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: In the English dub, Jiji was voiced by comedian Phil Hartman.

facts_and_myths.claim: Jiji flies with Kiki on her broom.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Jiji rides along on Kiki's broom as she flies around the town making deliveries.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Jiji once pretends to be a stuffed toy cat to help Kiki finish a delivery.

name: Arrietty
visual_anchor: A tiny girl in a red dress with a clothespin in her hair, carrying a sugar cube among giant green leaves in a sunny garden, 9:16 vertical shot.
core_traits: Tiny girl only a few inches tall
Lives secretly under the floor of a house
Borrows small things humans won't miss
Star of a 2010 Studio Ghibli film

facts_and_myths.claim: Arrietty's story is based on the book The Borrowers.
facts_and_myths.explanation: The film adapts The Borrowers, a children's novel by English author Mary Norton.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Arrietty clips her hair with a clothespin, which is huge for someone her size.

facts_and_myths.claim: Borrowers take big things like furniture from humans.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Borrowers only take tiny things humans won't miss, like a sugar cube or a pin.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: In the United States, the film was released as The Secret World of Arrietty.

name: Baron Humbert von Gikkingen
visual_anchor: An elegant cat gentleman in a smart suit, top hat and bow tie, holding a walking cane in a tiny cozy town square at golden sunset, 9:16 vertical shot.
core_traits: Elegant cat gentleman in a top hat and suit
Started as a cat figurine in an antique shop
Appears in Whisper of the Heart
Runs the Cat Bureau in The Cat Returns

facts_and_myths.claim: The Baron appears in two Studio Ghibli movies.
facts_and_myths.explanation: He first appears as a figurine in Whisper of the Heart, then comes to life in The Cat Returns.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Whisper of the Heart came out in 1995, and The Cat Returns in 2002.

facts_and_myths.claim: The Baron is a real cat who lives in a pet shop.
facts_and_myths.explanation: In Whisper of the Heart, the Baron is a cat figurine sitting in an antique shop.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: In The Cat Returns, the Baron helps a girl named Haru who can talk to cats.

name: Hamtaro
visual_anchor: A cute orange-and-white hamster with big shiny eyes, nibbling a sunflower seed on a sunny windowsill, 9:16 vertical shot.
core_traits: Small orange-and-white hamster
Loves sunflower seeds
Lives with a girl named Laura in the English version
Goes on adventures with his friends, the Ham-Hams

facts_and_myths.claim: Hamtaro's best friends are a group called the Ham-Hams.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Hamtaro sneaks out to meet the Ham-Hams, who gather in their own secret clubhouse.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The Ham-Hams greet each other with a cheerful 'Hamha!'

facts_and_myths.claim: Hamtaro lives in the wild woods.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Hamtaro is a pet hamster who lives with his owner and sneaks out for adventures while she is at school.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The Hamtaro cartoon began as a Japanese picture book series about a little hamster.

name: Chi
visual_anchor: A tiny gray-and-white striped kitten with big curious eyes, sitting in a cozy apartment next to a ball of yarn, 9:16 vertical shot.
core_traits: Tiny gray-and-white striped kitten
Got lost from her mother during a walk
Adopted by the Yamada family and their little boy Yohei
Star of the manga and anime Chi's Sweet Home

facts_and_myths.claim: Chi was born in the Yamada family's home.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Chi got lost from her mother and siblings, and young Yohei found her in a park.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Each episode of the 2008 Chi's Sweet Home anime is only about three minutes long.

facts_and_myths.claim: The Yamadas first lived in an apartment where pets weren't allowed.
facts_and_myths.explanation: The family tried to keep Chi a secret, and later moved to a home where pets are welcome.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Chi's Sweet Home was created by manga artist Konami Kanata.

name: Agumon
visual_anchor: A small, friendly orange dinosaur creature with big green eyes, standing proudly on a sunny grassy hill under a bright blue sky, 9:16 vertical shot.
core_traits: Small orange dinosaur-like creature
Has big green eyes and three-clawed hands
Partner of Tai Kamiya in Digimon Adventure
Digivolves into Greymon

facts_and_myths.claim: Agumon Digivolves into Greymon.
facts_and_myths.explanation: When Tai needs help, Agumon Digivolves into Greymon, a much bigger dinosaur Digimon.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The name Digimon is short for 'Digital Monsters.'

facts_and_myths.claim: Digimon is just another name for Pokemon.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Digimon and Pokemon are separate franchises with different creatures, stories and creators.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Digimon began in 1997 as a virtual pet toy, similar to a Tamagotchi.

name: Jibanyan
visual_anchor: A chubby red cartoon cat with two tails and a yellow bell on its belly band, happily holding a chocolate bar in a colorful park, 9:16 vertical shot.
core_traits: Chubby red cat with two tails
Wears a belly band with a yellow bell
Loves chocolate bars called Chocobars
Famous yo-kai friend of Nate in Yo-kai Watch

facts_and_myths.claim: Jibanyan has two tails.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Jibanyan is a cat yo-kai, and his two tails are one of his best-known features.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Jibanyan's special move is called Paws of Fury.

facts_and_myths.claim: Real cats can safely eat chocolate bars like Jibanyan.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Chocolate is not safe for real cats or dogs. Only cartoon cats like Jibanyan can snack on it.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Yo-kai Watch was created by Level-5, the game studio behind Professor Layton.

name: Chibi Maruko-chan
visual_anchor: A cheerful little cartoon girl with a short bob haircut and a red skirt, walking home from school past green tea fields with Mount Fuji in the distance, 9:16 vertical shot.
core_traits: Cheerful, lazy-but-lovable third-grade girl
Has a short bob haircut and wears a red skirt
Lives with her parents, big sister and grandparents
Her story is set in Shizuoka, Japan, in the 1970s

facts_and_myths.claim: Chibi Maruko-chan is based on its creator's own childhood.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Manga artist Momoko Sakura based Maruko's funny school days on her own memories of growing up.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Maruko's real name is Momoko Sakura, the same as her creator's pen name.

facts_and_myths.claim: Chibi Maruko-chan is set in modern-day Tokyo.
facts_and_myths.explanation: The story takes place in Shimizu, a town in Shizuoka, Japan, during the 1970s.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Maruko's grandpa Tomozo is her biggest fan and often spoils her.

name: Luna the Cat
visual_anchor: A sleek black cat with a golden crescent moon mark on her forehead, sitting on a moonlit windowsill under twinkling stars, 9:16 vertical shot.
core_traits: Sleek black cat who can talk
Has a golden crescent moon on her forehead
Guides Usagi Tsukino on her adventures
Gave a magical brooch to the girl who became Sailor Moon

facts_and_myths.claim: Luna has a crescent moon mark on her forehead.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Luna's golden crescent moon shows that she comes from the ancient Moon Kingdom.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Luna gives Usagi the magical brooch that lets her transform into Sailor Moon.

facts_and_myths.claim: Luna is a white cat.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Luna is a black cat. Her white cat friend Artemis guides Sailor Venus.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The name Luna means 'moon' in Latin.

name: Ninja Hattori
visual_anchor: A cheerful young ninja boy in a blue ninja outfit leaping across tiled rooftops with a small light-brown puppy, bright blue sky, 9:16 vertical shot.
core_traits: Young ninja boy in a blue outfit
Lives with his friend Kenichi Mitsuba
Has a ninja puppy named Shishimaru
Created by Fujiko Fujio, the duo behind Doraemon

facts_and_myths.claim: Ninja Hattori comes from the same manga duo as Doraemon.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Both were published under the pen name Fujiko Fujio, a famous duo of manga artists.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Hattori's puppy Shishimaru loves chikuwa, a tube-shaped Japanese fish cake.

facts_and_myths.claim: Ninja Hattori is a grown-up ninja.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Hattori is a young ninja boy, about the same age as his best friend Kenichi.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Ninja Hattori became hugely popular with kids in India.

name: Beyblade
visual_anchor: Two colorful spinning-top toys whirling inside a bowl-shaped plastic stadium while smiling kids cheer in the background, 9:16 vertical shot.
core_traits: Toy spinning tops built for friendly contests
Launched into a bowl-shaped stadium
The last top still spinning wins
The 2001 anime starred Tyson Granger and his Dragoon

facts_and_myths.claim: Players shout 'Let it rip!' when launching their Beyblades.
facts_and_myths.explanation: 'Let it rip!' became the famous launch call in the Beyblade anime and toy commercials.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Beyblade was inspired by beigoma, traditional Japanese spinning tops.

facts_and_myths.claim: A Beyblade can keep spinning forever once it is launched.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Friction with the stadium floor slowly steals its energy, so every Beyblade eventually wobbles and stops.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Beyblades are made by the Japanese toy company Takara Tomy.
